This atlas is a history of AI safety research from the 1950s to 2026, told alongside reinforcement learning and agents, neural networks and language models, and the institutions that fund, build and govern AI. Each has a lane on the map below.

For most of that time the first three were separate fields. They met between 2017 and 2022, when a reward model trained on people's comparisons, first tested on Atari games and a simulated robot, became part of the method behind InstructGPT and ChatGPT. Reward hacking, long seen in game-playing agents, and deceptive alignment, until then mostly argued on paper, became things researchers could test on language models.

## About this atlas

The atlas concentrates on alignment and catastrophic-risk research, and most of its institutional coverage is American and British. Almost half of the safety entries from 2023 on are Anthropic's, so the recent years lean towards one lab's work.

I made the atlas with extensive help from Claude Code and Codex. AI agents wrote most of the cards and checked their dates and sources; I directed the selection and edited the result. Each card lists its sources. Where a card rests mainly on a company's report about its own model, the card says so.

Corrections and missing work are welcome as [issues on GitHub](https://github.com/sergeisoly/sergeisoly.github.io/issues). Last updated 8 November 2026.
